properties.name: Recording an open question must never assert that it was settled
properties.statement: A Decision's status must not be set on the user's behalf. Recording a choice someone is still facing — an open question, a brainstormed option, a decision point held for later — must land as `proposed`, and reaching `accepted` must be a separate, deliberate act. Found as friction 2026-07-25: add_decision defaults to `accepted`, so six open questions recorded in one session each landed as settled and needed correcting immediately afterwards. This generalises dec:certainty-derived from requirements to decisions, and the reason is the same: an accepted Decision is what where-am-i reads back to the user as "what you decided", what the fork layer treats as binding, and what the KPP contradiction check reads as a trade already made. A musing recorded as a reasoned choice is therefore worse than a missing record — it is a false one, attributed to them. Evidence it was systemic rather than one slip: the correction had become a standing note carried across sessions, and the brainstorm skill had to instruct it in prose ("this call is not optional"), which is a defect with a bandage on it.
